A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RewardMap work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable, and retained content can be matched reliably across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original fine-tuning experiments, benchmark evaluations, component ablations, qualitative comparisons, and training-reward trajectories.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds baseline evaluations, reward-weight sensitivity studies, Kimi-VL training results, and further benchmark findings.

M1.justification: Section 4 retains the same difficulty-weighted format, correctness, and detail rewards and the same staged GRPO curriculum. Algorithm 1 is unchanged. Additional annotation documentation and experiments do not establish a revised method.

E1.justification: Appendix E adds reported evaluations on Charxiv and InfoVQA, extending coverage to additional chart and infographic data. REASONMAP, REASONMAP-PLUS, and the six original external benchmarks remain.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds GPT-4o and GPT-5 reference models and REINFORCE++ and ReMax training baselines. This substantially broadens both reference-model and RL-algorithm comparisons. Existing comparators remain; the original single-dataset RL baseline is relabeled GRPO.

E3.justification: New experiments vary alpha over 0.3, 0.5, and 0.7, separately vary map/question reward weights, and train Kimi-VL-A3B-Instruct on REASONMAP training data. Existing splits, metrics, optimizer settings, and decoding procedures are retained.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained component and curriculum ablations, v2 adds reward-weight sensitivity studies in Tables 6–7 and architecture-transfer testing in Table 9. Section 5.2 analyzes gains by task category, and Appendix D.1 adds a counting-error comparison.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The training-reward visualization retains the same reporting practice.

E6.justification: Original numerical results remain, including the 72.27% six-benchmark average. v2 adds comparator, sensitivity, Kimi-training, and task-level results. Appendix E newly reports Charxiv improving from 66.41% to 68.90% and InfoVQA from 82.22% to 82.71%; these are additional reported evaluations, not revisions to v1 scores.

T1.justification: The centered group advantage, policy objective, reward equation, and piecewise difficulty-weight definitions are unchanged. No new formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same dataset, reward-design, curriculum, and generalization claims, including the headline 3.47% improvement across six benchmarks. Additional experiments support the existing contributions.

C2.justification: Section 5.4 newly interprets the sensitivity results as tolerance to reasonable reward-weight choices and the Kimi results as applicability beyond Qwen. Appendix E adds discussion of structurally similar domains, domain-agnostic rewards, efficiency, and safety-related future applications.

D1.justification: New Appendix A.3 documents route–stop JSON metadata, script-based process-annotation generation, and concrete annotated examples. Table 7 specifies training-weight configurations. These improve documentation without establishing changes to the existing data-generation procedure; hardware and access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 expands its RL positioning to curriculum and structured language-model reasoning, including Curriculum RL and Logic-RL. The introduction and Appendix E substantially expand citations across driving, 3D grounding, compression, other applications, and safety; new baseline and benchmark references are also added.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section sequence remain. Changes include a localized related-work rewrite, Method becoming Methodology, conference-header updates, new diagnostic and appendix subsections, acknowledgements, and relocation of the LLM-usage statement from Appendix D to F.

P2.justification: The empirical display expands through additional Table 1 rows and new Tables 6, 7, and 9. Appendices add metadata, annotation, and contrasting-answer boxes. Existing figures are retained, while the original model-scale table is relocated and renumbered from Table 6 to Table 8.

improvement.justification: New RL comparisons and sensitivity tests strengthen empirical scrutiny, while Appendix A.3 clarifies annotation construction. The gains are qualified: Table 9 uses REASONMAP-only training, limiting evidence for transfer of the full multi-stage curriculum, and Appendix E supplies little protocol detail for Charxiv and InfoVQA. Overall, v2 provides useful incremental validation and documentation.
